timeline.keys: Arrow keys move the playhead; once a clip is selected (click, tap, or Enter to pick the clip at the playhead) they move the selection between clips and Alt with arrows steps the playhead. Shift with arrows steps a second. S splits at the playhead, Delete removes the selection, comma and period nudge it a frame, left and right brackets trim its start or end to the playhead, Alt with comma or period trims its end by a frame (add Shift for its start), Control or Command with Z undoes and with Shift redoes, Escape clears the selection, plus and minus zoom, 0 fits the project, Page Up and Page Down scroll, Up and Down arrows scroll tracks.

diag.title: Device check
diag.intro: See what your device can do and how fast it is. The test takes about a minute. Everything runs on this device: nothing is uploaded and no account is needed.
diag.test.heading: Speed test
diag.test.hint: Keep this page open and in front while it runs. If you are sending us the result, tap Run, wait for it to finish, then tap Copy results.
diag.progress.label: Overall progress
diag.copy.ok: Copied. Paste it into your message.
diag.copy.manual: Your browser blocked copying: the text below is selected, copy it by hand.
diag.copy.idle: Then paste it into your message to us.
diag.caps.heading: What this device supports
diag.caps.error: The engine could not report this device: {message}. The speed test can still run.
diag.issues: Things that may limit you here
diag.t.decode.title: Playing HD video
diag.t.decode.what: How fast your device can unpack full-HD (1080p) video. The faster, the smoother playback and the quicker imports.
diag.t.seek.title: Jumping around in a video
diag.t.seek.what: How long it takes to show a frame when you drag the playhead to a random spot. Lower is snappier scrubbing.
diag.t.gpuUpload.title: Sending frames to the graphics chip
diag.t.gpuUpload.what: How fast a video frame reaches the graphics chip, the step before any effect is drawn. Several routes are tried on every graphics API the device has (WebGPU and WebGL2); the quickest one counts.
diag.t.playback.title: Playback, 1080p with 3 layers
diag.t.playback.what: Plays a generated full-HD 30 fps clip with 3 stacked layers for about 5 seconds through the real preview, and counts the frames shown and dropped.
diag.t.exportSpeed.title: Export speed
diag.t.exportSpeed.what: Exports a generated 10 second full-HD 30 fps clip with sound through the real exporter (default format) and reports how many times faster than real time it ran.
diag.t.fillRate.title: Drawing layers (effects speed)
diag.t.fillRate.what: How many full-HD layers of effects the graphics chip can draw per frame. More layers means room for titles, overlays and effects.
diag.s.timeout: This test took too long and was stopped. That is itself a sign of a slow device.
diag.s.decode: {fps} full-HD frames per second (a smooth video needs 30 to 60).
diag.s.seek: Typical jump: {a} ms on an editor-friendly video, {b} ms on a phone-style video (worst 1 in 20: {c} ms).
diag.s.gpuUpload: Quickest route: {best}. All routes, per frame: {all}.
diag.s.playback: {fps} frames per second ({presented} shown, {dropped} dropped) on {backend}, frames sent to the graphics chip by: {path}.
diag.s.exportSpeed: {x}x real time ({codec}); 1 means a 10 second video takes 10 seconds.
